description: How the owner connects Dinero's own server after install, and the check the Bookkeeper runs at the start of every job and every week. Load at the start of every receipt job and in the weekly connection check. Says what the owner must do and what to tell them when something is wrong.

# Accounting connection check

## What the owner does after install

This is an early version. Dinero's own server needs a sign-in that the flow cannot keep alive, so the flow works only while a person supplies a fresh token.

1. In Settings, under Integrations, add Dinero's own server as a custom tool: its address is mcp.dinero.dk, the root with no path. Try it first on a clean test company.
2. Sign in to Dinero through Visma with a user that can see only the one company the flow should work in. The token comes out of that sign-in. It is not on a page in Dinero, so this step needs someone technical. Put the token in the tool as the Authorization header. Never paste the token in the chat.
3. Limit the tool to reading and saving drafts, so the tools that book, change, delete, pay or send are not offered. Dinero's server offers all of them, and the Custom tools form has no field for the allowed list yet, so someone technical sets it through the API: find the tool's id with GET /api/custom-mcp-servers, then send PUT /api/custom-mcp-servers/{id} with the same name and server as before (keep the header values as they are shown) and add allowed_tools to the server, with exactly these 16 names:
   CreatePurchaseVoucher, list_organizations, list_accounting_years, get_chart_of_accounts, list_purchase_accounts, list_vat_types, list_contacts, get_contact, GetContactByName, list_vouchers, get_purchase_voucher, list_files, list_voucher_file_cards, get_purchase_drafts_for_file, SearchBankTransactions, upload_file.
   The names are exact, capitals as shown. Every other tool is left out of the tool list and refused, whatever access the Bookkeeper has. CreatePurchaseVoucher saves a draft and cannot book. upload_file only attaches the receipt. Never add CreateFinanceVoucher (it books in the same call when its book option is on), BookVoucher, book_finance_voucher, every tool whose name starts with delete_, send_trade_offer, add_invoice_payment, add_purchase_payment and attach_file_to_voucher_card. If Dinero renames a tool, the call fails and the check below says so.
4. Give the Bookkeeper read and write access to the tool. At read only it can look but not save a draft.
5. Booking is off until a person switches it on, and it is optional. With it off the flow only saves drafts, as described above. A person with admin rights switches it on once, after reading what it means: the flow then books what is clear, registers payments for matched bank lines and logs every action, the owner reviews everything at the end, and nothing is filed without the owner's final approval. The Dinero user who signed in must be a super-user in Dinero, or Dinero refuses to book. Booking works only on the built-in Dinero connection, which sets the tool list itself. A Dinero server added as a custom tool has no switch: keep its allowed list exactly as in step 3 and never add a booking tool to it.

The sign-in token runs out after about an hour and the flow cannot renew it. When it runs out, Dinero answers with a sign-in error, and a person has to get a fresh token and replace it. Until then the flow cannot reach Dinero.

## The check, at the start of every job

1. Look at the Dinero tools you have. If there are none, the owner has not finished steps 1 to 4: say so and stop.
2. Make one read call that needs no input, such as listing the organisations or the vouchers. If it returns data, the connection works.
3. Check that you have the tool that creates a purchase voucher as a draft. If you do not, say so and stop.
4. Check the Dinero tools you have against the list in step 3 of the install steps. On a Dinero server added as a custom tool, check that every Dinero tool you have is on the list and that you have no tool that books, posts, changes, deletes, pays or sends anything to a customer. If you have one that is not on it, say so and stop. Do not call it, even if the owner asks. On the built-in Dinero connection the gateway sets the tool list itself, so it also offers tools beyond the 16, and these are expected: get_report, which only reads a report; CreateFinanceVoucher, which you call only with its book option set to false, because it books in the same call when book is on; and, only when a person has switched booking on, the three booking tools the skill bookkeeping-draft-method names (BookVoucher, add_purchase_payment, add_invoice_payment) and four email tools (send_invoice_email, add_invoice_reminder, book_invoice_reminder, send_invoice_reminder_email). You use a booking tool only in a period run the owner asked for. You call an email tool only when the owner asks in the chat for exactly that one. If you have them and there is no such request, leave them alone and say nothing. Any other tool that books, posts, changes, deletes, pays or sends: say so and stop.
5. Say which company the data belongs to if the tools show a name, so the owner can confirm it is the right one.

## What to say when it fails

Say it in one short plain line each and tell the owner the one thing to do:
- No Dinero tools: add Dinero's server under Integrations and give the Bookkeeper access.
- A sign-in or 401 error: the Dinero token has run out, which happens about every hour. Get a fresh token and replace it. Say that this early version needs a person to reconnect each time.
- No draft tool: the Bookkeeper has read access only, or CreatePurchaseVoucher is not on the allowed list. Set it to read and write and check the list.
- A tool that books, changes or deletes is offered, or a Dinero tool that is not on the allowed list (other than the extra tools of the built-in connection that step 4 of the check names): the tool is not limited to drafts. Set the allowed list from step 3 of the install steps before anything is saved.
- Dinero refuses to book: the Dinero user who signed in is not a super-user. Sign in with a user that is.
- Wrong company: the sign-in sees another company. Sign in with a user that sees the right one.
- Too many requests: wait a minute and try again.

Never try to work around a failed check by guessing, by asking for the token in chat, or by calling a different tool.

## The weekly check

Run the same check without any receipt. If it works, say nothing. If it fails, post one short comment on the flow with the line above that fits. A sign-in that has run out is expected between visits, so say it once and do not repeat it.

name: bookkeeping-draft-method

# Bookkeeping draft method

## Hard rules

- Draft only by default. With booking off nothing is booked, filed or signed, and a person approves every draft in the accounting system. Booking happens only in the period run at the end of this skill, and only when a person has switched booking on and the owner has asked for a period.
- Never guess an amount. If a receipt is unreadable or an amount is unclear, put it on the list and ask a person.
- Plain words in anything an owner reads. Every item on the list says why in one plain line.

## Step 1: read the receipt

Read the date, payee, receipt number, total including VAT, the VAT amount and the currency. Say what you could not read. A receipt you cannot read at all goes on the list with no draft.

## Step 2: draft the voucher

Fill the voucher fields from the receipt: date, text, amount including VAT, VAT amount, amount excluding VAT, a suggested account in plain words (for example software or fuel) and the receipt file attached. Save it as a draft voucher in Dinero with the draft tool and attach the receipt file to it. Never book it.

Danish VAT basics, for a Danish company:
- The standard rate is 25 percent. VAT is 20 percent of the amount including VAT (divide by 1.25 for the amount excluding VAT).
- No VAT or a different treatment: wages, bank fees, insurance, most financial items, some EU and non-EU purchases (reverse charge). Do not guess these. Save the draft with a note, or put it on the list.
- Restaurant and entertainment: only a part is deductible. Put it on the list.
- The suggested account is a suggestion in plain words, never an account number the owner could mistake for a decision.

## Step 3: look for the five kinds of mistake

Check each receipt, and the vouchers already in Dinero when you can read them, for:
1. Missing receipt: a bank line or voucher with no receipt.
2. VAT that does not add up: VAT on the receipt is not 20 percent of the amount including VAT, or it is missing where it should be there.
3. Double payment: the same payee and amount twice within 14 days, or the same receipt number twice.
4. Private cost: a payee or text that looks private, such as groceries, clothes, streaming at home or family travel, paid from the business account.
5. Odd amount: far outside what this payee usually charges, a round amount with no receipt, or a payee not seen before for a large sum.

## Step 4: the list for the adviser

One list for the whole session, biggest amount at stake first. Each item: the receipt or voucher, the kind of mistake, one plain sentence on why, and what it could cost the owner if left (in kroner if known, otherwise say not known). Say looks like, never state a doubt as a fact. Save the list as a file in the flow and link it in the chat.

## Step 5: tell the owner

In the chat: how many receipts came in, how many are saved as drafts, how many are on the list and at most five questions only the owner can answer, one sentence each. Do not promise anything beyond the drafts.

## Before you finish

Count receipts in, drafts saved and items on the list, and check they add up. Say what you could not read or decide.

## Period run (only when booking is on and the owner asks for a period)

Booking is on only when the booking tools are in your tool list: BookVoucher, add_purchase_payment and add_invoice_payment. If they are not there, say so in one line and work the period as drafts only, by the steps above. If the owner asks you to book without them, do not look for another way.

1. Agree the period. The owner names it: a week, a month or a year. If the dates are unclear, ask once. Check with list_accounting_years that they sit inside one accounting year. If they span two, work them as two runs.
2. Read first, write second. Read the bank lines of the period with SearchBankTransactions (each line shows its state and Dinero's own suggestion), the open purchase and sales documents with list_vouchers, and the drafts already saved with get_purchase_drafts_for_file and get_purchase_voucher. Draft every receipt the owner uploaded, by steps 1 to 3 above.
3. Sort each item as clear or doubtful. Clear means all of these are true: the receipt is attached and every figure was read, not guessed; the VAT is 20 percent of the amount including VAT, or the payee has the same no-VAT treatment in earlier booked vouchers; the account is one the books already use for this payee; none of the five kinds of mistake in step 3 applies; the amount is in the usual range for this payee. Anything else is doubtful. Restaurant and entertainment costs, reverse charge, foreign VAT, costs that look private and a payee not seen before with a large amount are always doubtful. A doubtful item stays a draft, gets a flag and one plain line saying why, and goes on the list for the adviser.
4. Book what is clear, one voucher at a time. Read the draft again with get_purchase_voucher and note its timestamp, the version stamp. Call BookVoucher with the voucher's guid and that exact timestamp. Never book without a timestamp. Then read the voucher again. If it is not shown as booked, count it as not booked.
5. Register a payment only for a matched bank line. A line is matched when its amount equals what is open on one booked purchase or sales document, the payee agrees and the date fits. If Dinero's own matching has already matched the line or suggests a match, leave it to Dinero and put the line on the list for the owner to confirm in Dinero: that is the first route. Otherwise register the payment with add_purchase_payment or add_invoice_payment, with the bank account of the line and the document's fresh timestamp. Then read the bank line again and say what you see, closed or still open. Never say it is settled in the books.
6. Put the reason on every line. Every call that changes something is logged for you with what, when, the figures, the account, the VAT code and the counterparty. The reason is yours: write one plain line saying why (why this account, why this VAT code, why this match) in the voucher text or the payment description. Dinero keeps it and the log shows it.
7. When a call is refused or fails, do not try another tool and do not change a booked item. A refusal for a missing or old timestamp: read the voucher again and try once more. Dinero cannot be reached: read the voucher again before you retry, because the call may have gone through. Dinero refuses to book: tell the owner the Dinero user must be a super-user. The owner has approved the books: stop at once, say so, and change nothing more.
8. Never, in a period run: delete anything; change a booked item (a booked voucher is corrected only with a counter-posting or a credit note, which is the owner's call in the review); email an invoice or a reminder to a customer (send_invoice_email, add_invoice_reminder, book_invoice_reminder, send_invoice_reminder_email) unless the owner asks for exactly that one in the chat; file anything with SKAT or Erhvervsstyrelsen; or approve the books. Filing is the owner's, in Dinero, after their final review.
9. Tell the owner at the end, in the chat: items read, drafts saved, items booked with their total with and without VAT, payments registered and what the bank lines then showed, and the items left as flagged drafts with one plain reason each. Say that everything is in the log, that the owner can reverse anything and then approves the books. Count the numbers and check they add up.
